newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: South Australia calls for national tax review.
newsitem.headline: South Australia calls for national tax review.

text.p: The federal government should establish a major review of Australia's tax system which should go beyond just a move to a goods and services tax (GST), the South Australian government said on Wednesday.

"The Commonwealth should establish a major review of Australia's tax system, along the lines of the Wallis and Campbell inquiries into Australia's banking and financial system," South Australian Premier John Olsen told a business lunch.

Olsen said tax reform was much more than a move to a GST and that former Liberal leader John Hewson's GST agenda, widely attributed to the Opposition's loss in the 1992 election, was "far too narrow a thrust".
"The much wider tax reform we require must consider the impact of the tax system (on) economic activity, especially national productivity and international competitiveness," he said.
"The current system...is as controversial and as irrelevant as it is prohibitive to growth, to individual effort, to industry competitiveness and to a raised standard of living," he said.

Olsen targeted the wholesale sales tax which he said not only worked against manufacturing but against states, chiefly South Australia and Victoria, which were reliant on that sector ahead of exempt sectors like tourism, telecommunications, financial services and mining.
"Australia's taxation policies have become a dead weight on the back of manufacturing," he said.

Olsen said state governments' reliance on income from gaming activities, which had been criticised by the federal government, was a direct consequence of the States' search for an expanded revenue base and the Commonwealth's failure to enter into any realistic commitment on revenue sharing.
Being able to achieve taxation reform was the real test of national maturity and leadership as Australia moved into the next century, he said.
